title: Four kinds of people who turn to God

verses.sa: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
verses.tr: My divine illusion, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross. Only those who take refuge in Me go beyond it.
verses.angle: duratyaya, hard to cross, names the obstacle
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names the obstacle and the only way past it. Listen for the one word that tells you exactly how hard the battle is.

body.text: My divine illusion, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross. Only those who take refuge in Me go beyond it. The word is duratyaya, hard to cross. Krishna says his maya, made of the three gunas, is duratyaya, and only those who surrender to him can cross beyond it. Krishna then explains that the deluded and wrongdoers do not surrender to him, but take refuge in a shadowed nature instead.

verses.sa: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः । माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
verses.tr: The deluded, the lowest among people, the wrongdoers, and those whose understanding has been stolen by the veil do not turn to me. They take refuge in a shadowed nature instead.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Right after Krishna says only those who take refuge in him can cross the veil, he names the ones who never will. Listen to how he describes the minds that stay trapped.

body.text: The deluded, the lowest among people, the wrongdoers, and those whose understanding has been stolen by the veil do not turn to me. They take refuge in a shadowed nature instead. Here is one word, apahrita-jnana, whose understanding has been stolen. The veil does not just confuse them; it takes their knowledge away, so they cannot even look toward the truth. Krishna now turns to the other side of the same gate, naming the four kinds of people who do seek him out.

verses.sa: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.tr: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas.
verses.angle: Four types of people seeking refuge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues, naming the four kinds of virtuous people who still turn to him. Listen to the four reasons that bring them to his feet.

body.text: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas. Krishna names four kinds, and the last one, the wise, is the highest. The distressed come for relief, the curious for answers, the wealthy for gain, and the wise for union. Krishna now crowns the wise devotee as the best, saying they are dear to him above all others.

verses.sa: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते । प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
verses.tr: Among those four, the wise devotee who is ever united and one-pointed is श्रेष्ठ. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and the wise one is dear to me.
verses.angle: Krishna crowns the ever-united, one-pointed devotee
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just named four kinds of devotees. Now he answers which one he values most. Listen for the one he calls distinguished.

body.text: Among those four, the wise devotee who is ever united and one-pointed is श्रेष्ठ. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and the wise one is dear to me. Krishna singles out the wise devotee who is nityayukta, ever united and devoted to only him. He says this kind of love is mutual. Krishna goes further, saying this wise devotee is not only dear to him, but is his very self.

verses.sa: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: All these are noble indeed, but the wise devotee is My very self. Established in yoga, that person is steadfast in Me as the unsurpassed goal.
verses.angle: The wise one is my very self
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just praised four kinds of people who turn to him. Now he raises the highest one and reveals the secret of union.

body.text: All these are noble indeed, but the wise devotee is My very self. Established in yoga, that person is steadfast in Me as the unsurpassed goal. Krishna calls all four noble, then says the wise devotee is his very self, fixed on him alone as the highest goal. He adds that such a wise one is very rare, having come only after many births of seeking.

verses.sa: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते । वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥
verses.tr: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
verses.angle: Deep seeing ends in surrender to the one reality in all things.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now says that the wise one who sees the divine everywhere and surrenders is very rare. Listen for that word.

body.text: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare. Vasudeva is the name of the divine, and it means the one who dwells everywhere. The wise one who sees that Vasudeva is everything and surrenders is what Krishna calls rare. Krishna then explains that those whose understanding is clouded by desire turn to other radiant beings instead.

verses.sa: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः । तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
verses.tr: Driven by desire, people whose understanding has been taken away turn to other radiant beings. They follow the rules of each, shaped by their own nature.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After describing the rare soul who surrenders to the supreme reality, Krishna now explains the opposite path. Listen to who takes refuge instead.

body.text: Driven by desire, people whose understanding has been taken away turn to other radiant beings. They follow the rules of each, shaped by their own nature. Krishna names the root cause of the error: hrit-jnanah, those whose understanding is taken away by desire. It is not a lack of knowledge, but a theft of the mind. He then says that whatever form a devotee chooses, he makes that faith firm and lasting.

verses.sa: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
verses.tr: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers why people turn to different gods: he is the one who steadies the faith behind each form. Listen for the word that means making faith firm.

body.text: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form. Whatever form a devotee worships with faith, Krishna says he himself makes that faith steady. That steady faith then leads the devotee to receive their desires, given by Krishna alone.

verses.sa: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते । लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान् ॥
verses.tr: Endowed with that faith, that person seeks that worship, and receives those desires, granted by Me alone.
verses.angle: Mayeva: Krishna alone grants the desires
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: A person worships a chosen god and gets a wish granted. Listen for who really hands over the reward.

body.text: Endowed with that faith, that person seeks that worship, and receives those desires, granted by Me alone. The word mayeva, by Me alone, means the deity is only the postman. The devotee asks the god for a boon, yet Krishna admits in this verse that he alone ordains every single one of those wishes. Krishna then draws a sharp line between the temporary rewards of these worshippers and the eternal reward of his own devotees.

verses.sa: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् । देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥
verses.tr: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is drawing a clear line here. Listen to how he sorts the results of worship.

body.text: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me. Krishna says those with limited understanding get limited rewards. Worshippers of the gods reach the gods. His devotees reach him. The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.

verses.sa: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः । परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥
verses.tr: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.
verses.angle: Avyakta, the unmanifest, is the source of his visible form
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks you to listen for one word that describes the true source of his human form.

body.text: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature. The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know that avyakta, the unmanifest, is the source from which this visible form came. Krishna then explains that he is hidden from the deluded by yoga-maya, his divine illusion.

verses.sa: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः । मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: Veiled by yoga-maya, I am not visible to everyone. Deluded people do not recognize me as unborn and imperishable.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains why he is hidden from ordinary eyes even while standing right before everyone. Listen for the reason he gives.

body.text: Veiled by yoga-maya, I am not visible to everyone. Deluded people do not recognize me as unborn and imperishable. The word yogamaya, yoga-maya, is the veil. It covers him so that the deluded, the confused, look and fail to see the immortal, unborn self. He then says he knows every being in all three times, past, present, and future. No one knows him.

verses.sa: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन । भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future. No one knows me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said he is hidden from ordinary sight. Now he tells Arjuna what that hiding means.

body.text: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future. No one knows me. Listen to the word vedah, I know. It is the first verb in the verse, and it carries the entire weight of the verse: Krishna knows every being, but no one knows him. O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.

verses.sa: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
verses.tr: O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now explains exactly what keeps a soul trapped in the cycle of birth and death. Listen for the pair of forces behind it.

body.text: O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes. The verse names the exact source of delusion, ichchha-dvesha, desire and aversion. These two opposing pulls create duhkha, and from that confusion, all beings are thrown into repeated birth and death. Krishna now tells Arjuna what happens when that confusion is finally cleared away.

verses.sa: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् । ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
verses.tr: But those whose wrongdoing has been cleared away, and whose good deeds have matured, are freed from confusion and worship me with firm resolve.
verses.angle: Freed from the confusion of opposites
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks of the people who have moved past the confusion of opposites. Listen for the state they reach.

body.text: But those whose wrongdoing has been cleared away, and whose good deeds have matured, are freed from confusion and worship me with firm resolve. Listen to dvandvamohanirmuktah, freed from the confusion of opposites. In this verse, people who have cleared away their wrongdoing and ripened their good deeds are no longer pulled between pleasure and pain. Krishna then explains that these people, seeking release from old age and death, come to know Brahman and all action.

verses.sa: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये । ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
verses.tr: Those who, seeking release from old age and death, take refuge in me, come to know Brahman, the whole field of the inner life, and all action.
verses.angle: Mamashritya: refuge in the person himself
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names the deepest human fear to show the path beyond it. Listen for the one who takes refuge in him.

body.text: Those who, seeking release from old age and death, take refuge in me, come to know Brahman, the whole field of the inner life, and all action. Those who take refuge in Krishna to escape old age and death come to know Brahman, self, and action. Krishna then tells how those who know him at the moment of death see the whole world differently.

verses.sa: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः । प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
verses.tr: Those who know me together with the physical realm, the radiant powers, and the inner sacrifice know me even at the time of death.
verses.angle: Complete understanding remains steady even at the moment of departure.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just explained the full structure of reality, and now he gives Arjuna a final key. Listen to how knowing him in three layers leads to reaching him at death.

body.text: Those who know me together with the physical realm, the radiant powers, and the inner sacrifice know me even at the time of death. Listen to the end of the verse. Those with a disciplined mind know me even at the time of death. The verse shows that knowing Krishna in matter, in the gods, and in sacrifice leads to knowing him at death. The next chapter begins with Arjuna asking Krishna to define the terms he has just used.
